The optimal time for acid suppression in Los Angeles (LA) grade C or D reflux oesophagitis has not been clearly established. However, studies suggest that successful healing of LA grade C or D oesophagitis typically occurs after 4 weeks' acid-suppressive therapy.

A noncomparative trial with a relatively short follow-up period found that patients who received acid suppression for an extended duration (up to 12 months) experienced improved outcomes compared to those who were switched to a different type of acid suppression or did not receive treatment at all. This suggests that optimal acid suppression may be achieved after a longer duration of therapy.

It is essential to note that the effectiveness of acid suppression in LA grade C or D oesophagitis can vary depending on individual patient factors, such as severity of symptoms and presence of comorbid conditions. A more comprehensive approach to managing reflux disease, including medical therapy, lifestyle modifications, and potential surgical interventions, may be necessary for optimal outcomes.

Overall, the current evidence suggests that acid suppression is essential for healing LA grade C or D oesophagitis, but the optimal time frame for treatment needs further clarification. Further research is needed to better understand the relationship between acid suppression duration and patient outcomes in this population.
